response.query: Precisely define core metrics: how will MMD be computed (kernel, bandwidth selection, per-domain vs global), how is spatial Dice for skeletons computed, what are AE localization error tolerances (units), and fracture-energy error definition?
response.answer: Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) uses kernel functions and adaptive bandwidth selection; spatial Dice for skeletons is computed using overlap metrics; AE localization error tolerances are typically in millimeters; fracture-energy error is defined by the difference in calculated vs. actual energy.

results.title: How to Implement Performance Metrics in CUDA C/C++ | NVIDIA Technical Blog
results.content: CUDA performance measurement is most commonly done from host code, and can be implemented using either CPU timers or CUDA-specific timers. Let’s take a look at the data transfers and kernel launch of the SAXPY host code from the previous post:. SAXPY reads 12 bytes per element computed, but performs only a single multiply-add instruction (2 FLOPs), so it’s pretty clear that it will be bandwidth bound, and so in this case (in fact in many cases), bandwidth is the most important metric to measure and optimize. This post described how to time kernel execution using the CUDA event API. CUDA events use the GPU timer and therefore avoid the problems associated with host-device synchronization. We presented the effective bandwidth and computational throughput performance metrics, and we implemented effective bandwidth in the SAXPY kernel. CUDA events can also be used to determine the data transfer rate between host and device, by recording events on either side of the `cudaMemcpy()` calls.
